journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for intent-driven network slice management in 5G and beyond environments. Traditional network management approaches rely on static policy definitions and reactive optimization, which struggle to cope with the dynamic nature of emerging network services. We propose an adaptive management paradigm where intent specifications are automatically translated into network configurations through hierarchical multi-agent coordination. Our theoretical analysis establishes the convergence properties of the proposed distributed learning algorithm under non-stationary network conditions. We formulate the management problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process and develop a attention-based communication protocol enabling agents to share relevant state information efficiently. Rigorous mathematical proofs demonstrate that our approach achieves O(1/T) regret bound, where T represents the time horizon. The paradigm shift lies in treating network management as a continuous learning process rather than a rule-based configuration task. Simulation results across diverse traffic scenarios show that our framework reduces intent fulfillment latency by 47% compared to state-of-the-art approaches while maintaining stability during high-load conditions. This work opens new research directions for applying cooperative multi-agent learning to comprehensive network and service management in complex telecommunication infrastructures.

This paper proposes an enhanced fault prediction mechanism for virtualized network functions (VNFs) leveraging improved temporal convolutional networks with attention-based anomaly detection. Existing fault management approaches in NFV environments suffer from limited temporal modeling capabilities and high false positive rates during resource contention scenarios. Our method introduces a novel feature extraction pipeline that combines network telemetry metrics with VNF-specific operational characteristics. We develop a lightweight attention mechanism that dynamically weights temporal dependencies based on failure correlation patterns observed in production environments. The theoretical analysis provides bounds on detection accuracy improvement derived from the proposed attention weighting scheme, demonstrating a reduction in false positive rate from 15.3% to 4.7% under equivalent recall conditions. We prove that the computational complexity remains O(n log n) for sequence length n, enabling real-time deployment. Extensive evaluation using real fault data from operational电信 networks demonstrates that our approach achieves 94.2% prediction accuracy within 5-minute lead time, representing a 23% improvement over existing solutions. The enhanced mechanism significantly improves network reliability management while maintaining acceptable computational overhead for large-scale deployments.

We present IntentFlow, a groundbreaking intent-driven network orchestration system that fundamentally transforms how network services are managed and delivered. Unlike conventional orchestration platforms that require detailed low-level specifications, IntentFlow interprets high-level business objectives and automatically synthesizes appropriate network configurations. The system architecture comprises three novel components: a natural language processing module for intent extraction, a knowledge graph-based policy reasoning engine, and a distributed execution framework with real-time monitoring capabilities. Our design introduces a feedback loop mechanism where network state changes trigger automatic intent re-evaluation, enabling self-healing and self-optimization behaviors. The system implements a domain-specific language allowing operators to specify complex service requirements while maintaining formal verification capabilities. We developed a complete prototype implementation integrating with OpenStack and Kubernetes ecosystems, demonstrating seamless interoperability with existing cloud management infrastructure. Evaluation in a production-like environment with 500+ network elements shows that IntentFlow reduces service provisioning time from hours to minutes while achieving 99.99% intent fulfillment accuracy. The paradigm shift enables non-expert users to manage complex networks through intuitive interfaces while providing network professionals with powerful automation capabilities.

This paper presents an enhanced distributed network management system architecture addressing scalability limitations in large-scale data center networks. Existing centralized management approaches exhibit performance degradation when handling millions of network elements, while current distributed solutions lack efficient coordination mechanisms. Our system introduces a hierarchical management framework with localized decision-making and global optimization coordination. We designed novel consensus protocols optimized for network configuration synchronization that reduce communication overhead by 60% compared to traditional approaches. The implementation includes adaptive load balancing that dynamically distributes management tasks based on network topology and traffic patterns. A key improvement is the incorporation of incremental verification ensuring configuration consistency without requiring full network-wide validation. We deployed the system across a 10,000-node testbed spanning multiple geographically distributed data centers. Experimental results demonstrate linear scalability up to 50,000 managed elements while maintaining sub-second configuration propagation latency. The enhanced system achieves 99.999% availability through novel fault-tolerant mechanisms that isolate failures without disrupting overall network operations. Performance measurements indicate 40% improvement in network operations efficiency and 35% reduction in operational overhead compared to existing commercial solutions.
